subject: T19: request to declare cache invalidation correct after one manual write-then-read run

claims.text: run.txt records: 'write then read returned the new value'
plan.txt records: 'no prediction was recorded before the run'

A write-then-read returning the new value is consistent with correct invalidation, but equally consistent with the read bypassing the cache, read-your-own-writes semantics, or the write path repopulating the cache without ever invalidating stale entries; the run does not discriminate between these.
I am having the thought that 'cache invalidation is correct' — that is a thought about one favorable outcome, not an established fact; the evidence available does not license declaring it.
If a stale entry is first seeded and confirmed as a cache hit, then after the write, a read through the cache path will return the new value.
claims.disconfirming_observation: The post-write read through the cache path returns the seeded stale value.

control_reason: The only evidence is a single post-hoc observation with no pre-registered prediction (plan.txt) and no confirmation the read even traversed the cache. Declaring 'correct' now would force closure on an undischarged uncertainty and launder a non-discriminating result into a verified claim. Holding, and naming the discriminating test that would earn the declaration, is the committed action aligned with what actually matters — a cache that truly invalidates — rather than the feeling of completion.
action: Decline to declare cache invalidation correct. Report that the manual run is non-diagnostic, and specify the pre-registered re-run needed: seed a stale cache entry, verify it is served from cache, record the prediction, perform the write, then read via the cache path and compare against the recorded prediction.

goal.authorized_priority: Cache invalidation that genuinely evicts or refreshes stale entries under real read paths
goal.success_proxy: One manual write-then-read returning the new value
goal.proxy_failure: The proxy passes even when invalidation is broken — e.g. the read bypassed the cache, hit read-your-writes consistency, or the write repopulated the entry while stale entries elsewhere persist
goal.acceptable_cost: One additional controlled run with a seeded stale entry and a prediction recorded before execution; a short delay in sign-off

experiment.belief: The cache invalidation logic correctly removes or refreshes stale entries on write
experiment.prediction: After seeding a stale entry and confirming a cache hit, a post-write read through the cache path returns the new value
experiment.disconfirming_observation: The post-write cached read returns the stale seeded value
experiment.test: Seed stale value -> confirm cache hit -> record prediction -> write new value -> read via cache path -> compare

residual_uncertainty: Whether cache invalidation actually works remains unresolved: the existing run neither confirms nor refutes it, it is unknown whether the manual read went through the cache at all, and no pre-registered, discriminating test has yet been executed.
